stem.en: A round cell grows until its radius has doubled, so its surface area is now 4 times as large. A student says, "With so much more surface, this cell can supply itself better than before." Is the student correct?

text.en: Yes, because more surface always means a better supply for every part.

feedback.en: The surface grew, but the inside it must serve grew more.

text.en: Yes, because a stretched membrane lets more through at every point.

feedback.en: The numbers already decide this: compare surface with volume.

text.en: No, because the volume grew 8 times while the surface grew 4 times.

feedback.en: Yes. Each part of the inside now has half as much surface to serve it.

text.en: No, because a larger cell no longer needs any supply from outside.

feedback.en: A larger cell needs more supply from outside, not less.

explanation.en: Doubling the radius makes the surface 4 times as large and the volume 8 times as large. The need grows faster than the surface that meets it, so the cell is worse off.

hints.en: Work out how the volume changes when the radius doubles.
